Write a Greenlandic TA file

Source: R/ta.R
write_ta.Rd

Writes a data frame to a Greenlandic TA file in the old layout (version 1) or the new 140-character layout (version 2). The layout must be named, since it has to match what the receiver reads.

Usage

write_ta(x, path, version)

Arguments

x

A data frame with the columns nrnr, trans, brch, bas, eng, det, afg, kbx and optionally moms. Other columns are an error.

path

Path to write to.

version

1 (old layout) or 2 (new 140-character layout).

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

Writes the nine fields nrnr, trans, brch, bas, eng, det, afg, moms and kbx in the positions read_ta() reads them from. If moms is absent, it is derived: NA where trans is "0100" or "0700" (no VAT in Greenland), 0 otherwise.

The file reads back unchanged. A fixed-width file has no delimiters, so a value wider than its field does not fail: it pushes every following field out of place, and the file still parses, into the wrong columns. write_ta() therefore refuses to write anything it cannot write exactly, and lists every offending value at once:

  • Numbers are right-aligned, with the fewest decimals that reproduce the value exactly, so whole numbers have none. A number whose exact form is wider than its field is an error, never rounded.

  • Text is left-aligned. Since read_ta() trims fields and reads blank fields and "NA" as NA, text that is too long, empty, "NA", or starts or ends with a space is an error.

  • NA is written as a blank field.

See also

read_ta(), which shows both layouts.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
write_ta(df, "ta.file", version = 2)
} # }
